title: Audit and document all CSS/styling sources
description: Map all style sources: scrappy.tcss, widget DEFAULT_CSS, Textual defaults. Document what each does.
notes:
## CSS Audit Complete

### Style Sources Found
1. **scrappy.tcss** (187 lines) - Main app stylesheet
2. **TaskProgressWidget DEFAULT_CSS** (task_progress.py:23-36) - Widget hiding/showing
3. **SelectableLog DEFAULT_CSS** (selectable_log.py:30-34) - Has `background: $surface` conflict with tcss

### Theme Variables (from ColorSystem)
- $border = #00FFFF (cyan) - derived from primary
- $border-blurred = #020202 (almost black)
- $primary = #00FFFF (cyan)
- $secondary = #0077ff (blue)

### Widget Hierarchy (chat_layout.py)
Container #output_container > SelectableLog #output
ActivityIndicator (Label)
TaskProgressWidget (Static)
Container #input_container > Label #input_prompt + TextArea #input
StatusBar > Vertical #status_content

### Key Finding: TextArea Focus Border NOT Overridden
TextArea has Textual default: `&:focus { border: tall $border; }`
Our tcss has: `TextArea { border: none; }`
**Problem:** `TextArea:focus` has higher specificity than `TextArea`
**Result:** Focus border (#00FFFF cyan) appears when TextArea focused!

### Previous Fix Attempt Failed
Commit 48a4038 added `*:focus { border: none; }`
This didn't work because `TextArea:focus` > `*:focus` in specificity

### Recommended Fix for scrappy-jvh
Add to scrappy.tcss:
```css
TextArea:focus {
    border: none;
}
```
close_reason: Audit complete. Found TextArea focus border as primary suspect. See notes for details.

title: Fix blue separator bar - root cause analysis
description: Identify exactly which widget/style creates the teal bar. Appears when agent starts. Need to trace the actual source, not guess.
notes:
## Root Cause Identified

The blue/teal separator bar comes from **TextArea focus border**.

### Technical Details
- Textual's TextArea DEFAULT_CSS has: `&:focus { border: tall $border; }`
- `$border` is derived from primary color = #00FFFF (cyan)
- Our `TextArea { border: none; }` doesn't override the focus state
- Specificity: `TextArea:focus` > `TextArea`

### Previous Fix Attempts
- `*:focus { border: none; }` failed due to specificity (TextArea:focus > *:focus)
- Adding border:none to other widgets (Static, Container, etc.) was irrelevant

### Solution Applied
Added to scrappy.tcss:
```css
TextArea:focus {
    border: none;
}
```

This matches the specificity of Textual's default rule and overrides it.
close_reason: Added TextArea:focus { border: none; } to override Textual default focus border. Please test.

title: Update pyproject.toml ruff config to new lint section format
Process all tool_calls from LLM response, not just first
description:
Currently NativeToolCallParser only processes the first tool call when LLMs return multiple:

**Location:** response_parser.py:430
```python
tool_call = response.tool_calls[0]  # Only first, rest discarded
```

**Opportunity:**
LLMs can return parallel tool calls (e.g., write 3 files at once). The infrastructure exists in LLMResponse.tool_calls (List[ToolCall]) but we throw away all but the first.

**Proposed Solution:**
1. Parse all tool_calls into a list of AgentActions
2. Execute them in sequence (parallel execution is separate - scrappy-d77)
3. Return combined results to agent loop

**Benefits:**
- Fewer LLM round-trips for multi-file operations
- Better matches LLM capabilities (Claude/GPT can return multiple tool calls)
- More efficient for scaffolding tasks

**Considerations:**
- Confirmation UX: batch confirm or individual?
- Error handling: fail-fast or continue?
- Audit logging for batched operations

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Parser returns all tool_calls, not just first
- [ ] Agent loop handles multiple actions per iteration (sequential)
- [ ] Confirmation prompt handles batched unsafe actions
- [ ] Tests for multi-tool-call responses
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove vestigial /synthesize and /delegate commands
description: Both commands are vestigial from pre-LiteLLM architecture. They assume direct provider access but LiteLLM Router abstracts providers away. Remove: multiprovider.py, command routing, help text, validators if unused elsewhere.

close_reason: Fixed: flush mechanism ensures plan renders before confirmation prompt, TaskExecutor refactored to use LLM service, removed [Recommended: provider] metadata display

title: Copy from SelectableLog fails during capture mode
description:
When a prompt is waiting for user input (capture mode), attempting to copy text from the log doesn't work.

**Symptom:** Normally, text can be selected and copied from the chat log to clipboard. When the prompt is active/capturing input, copy stops working entirely.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Copy (Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Shift+C) works on selected log text even when prompt is active
- [ ] Prompt input capture does not block clipboard operations

**To Reproduce:**
1. Run scrappy, get some output in the log
2. Start typing a prompt (prompt becomes active)
3. Try to select and copy text from the log above
4. Copy fails
close_reason: Fixed in main_screen.py - moved SelectableLog copy check before capture mode cancellation
